_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. 2026-09-28 reprint on press 4.32.5: the info-key exclusion in doctorExitForFailOn (doctorInfoKeys + doctorIsInfoKey) is now emitted natively, so doctor_verdict.go no longer defines it and only adds "db_path" to the native map by a one-line body edit in doctor.go; the placeholder refusal, the credential probe and the no-credential row are still connector-only and were re-applied by hand (the 4.32.5 doctor body moved the credentials branch behind cfg.AuthHeader()). Stays active. 2026-09-28 reprint review also cured two defects the SHIPPED v0.1.6 carried: doctorShippedBaseURL was set to https://api.hubapi.com, which is HubSpot's one real API root for every portal, so doctor refused to dial it and told every operator (real token included) 'FAIL API: base_url is still the shipped placeholder; set HUBSPOT_BASE_URL' - it is now empty, which disables only the exact-match rule; and api.hubapi.com answers GET / with a 302 to http://developers.hubspot.com, which the client refuses (https->http downgrade), so doctor rendered 'unreachable' and skipped the credential probe. doctorReachIsRefusedRedirect treats a refused redirect as the server answering. Receipt: with a real token doctor now reports 'OK Credentials: valid (verified with GET /crm/v3/objects/calls)' and a bad token 'HTTP 401'. doctor_verdict_test.go pins both directions.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For hubspot the manifest gained: HUBSPOT_BASE_URL, HUBSPOT_OWNER_EMAIL. server.json gained: HUBSPOT_BASE_URL, HUBSPOT_OWNER_EMAIL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: HUBSPOT_BASE_URL, HUBSPOT_OWNER_EMAIL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. 2026-09-28 reprint on press 4.32.5: the MCP server gained `--transport http` gated by HUBSPOT_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN (press #4360), so that variable is now declared on all three channels as an optional secret; the asserts below pin it. The 4.32.5 platform layer also reads PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, which the base rules carve back as operator input (operator_exact; servosity/threatlocker/auvik declare it), so it is declared on all three channels as an optional non-secret and pinned below. 4.32.5 also reads HUBSPOT_USER_AGENT (client.go and deliver.go, via cliutil.EnvOverride) to override the request User-Agent; it is declared on all three channels as an optional non-secret (datagate precedent) and pinned below.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: which_test.go's TestWhichIndex_ExistsAndIsWellFormed resolves the words before the first flag as the Cobra path and checks the flag against that command's flag set, so the curated `which` index may keep its `sync --with-history` entry
handfixes.why: The research-driven novel feature 'Sync with property history' is spelled `sync --with-history` in research.json and therefore in the generated which.go index; that is what an agent running `hubspot-cli which 'property history'` should be told. cli-printing-press 4.32.x added a generated test asserting every index Command resolves through cobra Find with nothing left over, which a flag can never satisfy, so the fresh tree's own test suite failed (generate --validate exit 3) until this hand-edit. Retro candidate for the press: either resolve flags in the emitted test or reject flag-bearing novel commands at research-ingest time.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: press: which_test.go.tmpl should strip flag tokens before cobra Find (or the research schema should carry the flag separately from the command path)

handfixes.summary: `sync --with-history <props>` asks HubSpot for propertiesWithHistory on meetings/deals/contacts/companies (capping the page at 50, the API's limit for that read) and persists per-property snapshots into hubspot_property_history via sync_history.go
handfixes.why: Every property-history novel command (meetings history / ever-had / status-report, deals velocity) reads the hubspot_property_history table that only this flag populates. The flag, the 50-row cap, the propertiesWithHistory/properties params and the per-item capture loop are body edits inside the generated sync.go (plus the extra trailing argument on both syncResource call sites, sync.go and channel_workflow.go); the helpers live in the hand-authored sync_history.go. Carried by hand through the 4.19 -> 4.22 -> 4.24 -> 4.32.5 reprints; recorded on the 2026-09-28 reprint so the next one notices instead of shipping a sync that silently ignores --with-history.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: press: a per-resource sync-hint for extra query params derived from a flag would let the spec carry this

handfixes.summary: The MCP server's streamable-HTTP listener sets ReadHeaderTimeout so one slow client cannot hold a connection open forever (gosec G112)
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32.x (#4360) added `<slug>-mcp --transport http` with bearer auth but constructs http.Server without ReadHeaderTimeout; the repo security gate reports it as P1 G112 (Slowloris) and does not honour inline #nosec, and the fleet suppression only covers the ephemeral OAuth-callback listener in auth.go. A ten-second header deadline is a real hardening, not a scanner workaround. Retro candidate for the press.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: press: set ReadHeaderTimeout in the generated MCP http.Server

handfixes.summary: Two 4.32.5-generated lines are reshaped so gosec stops mis-reading them: the HTTP bearer env-var NAME constant is called httpAuthEnvName (G101 keys on 'token' in the identifier), and the test sandbox's directory chmod uses a named os.FileMode const (G302 treats any literal above 0600 as a file mode) Press 4.34.0 names the HTTP token constant httpTokenEnvVar again (the fleet direction), so only the testenv part is carried.
handfixes.why: Both are false positives - a public env-var name and a 0700 DIRECTORY mode in a test-only package - but the repo security gate deliberately ignores inline #nosec and suppressions are CODEOWNERS-gated on main, so a reprint that regenerates these two lines goes red in CI until either the code is reshaped (this entry) or a base-policy suppression PR lands. If a fleet suppression for cli/cmd/<slug>-mcp/main.go G101 and cli/internal/cliutil/testenv/testenv.go G302 is ever added to tools/maintainer/security_suppressions.json, retire this entry and let the generated spelling stand.

handfixes.summary: `sync --full` prunes local rows only when the walk was unfiltered: any --param, --resource-param or --global-param disables deletion reconciliation (hsSyncPruneAllowed)
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32 made `sync --full` delete local rows the API did not return on a complete walk (prune := full && !noPrune). An operator query parameter can narrow the enumerated collection - `sync --resources hubspot-contacts-crm --full --param archived=true` lists only archived contacts - and pruning against that walk deletes every cached active contact (an empty archived set clears the mirror). The shipped 4.24 tree never pruned, so this was a regression the reprint introduced; found by the Codex review of the 2026-09-28 reprint. The one-line body edit in the generated sync.go routes the decision through the hand-authored hs_sync_prune.go; hs_sync_prune_test.go pins both directions (unfiltered full walk still prunes; each filter flag disables it).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: press: sync.go.tmpl should not prune a walk narrowed by operator --param/--resource-param/--global-param (or should reconcile only the filtered partition)

asserts.contains: prune := hsSyncPruneAllowed(full, noPrune, paramFlags, resourceParamFlags, globalParamFlags)

handfixes.summary: The remote-agent recipe runs `hubspot-mcp --transport http` with no --addr, so the 4.32.5 server's loopback default (127.0.0.1:7777) applies, and names the bearer header the HTTP transport requires
handfixes.why: msp-skills-publish emits `hubspot-mcp --transport http --addr :7777` into mcp-install.md, README.md and page.json (and from there docs/skills/hubspot.md). From press 4.32 the server refuses a non-loopback --addr without --tls-cert/--tls-key (`MCP server error: non-loopback --addr ":7777" requires --tls-cert and --tls-key`), so the documented command exits before the suggested tunnel can connect. Spelling it `--addr 127.0.0.1:7777` trips check_install_docs.py R3 (bare loopback origin), so the flag is dropped and the default does the binding. Found by the Codex review of the 2026-09-28 reprint; the same template line affects every 4.32.x connector. 2026-10-22: the remote-agent (HTTP mode) prose this entry guarded was removed on purpose when the interim security note paused HTTP mode until the reprint; restore those markers with the post-reprint docs fix.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: msp-skills-publish onboard template: emit `<slug>-mcp --transport http` (no --addr) for press >= 4.32 connectors and document the Authorization: Bearer <SLUG>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN header

handfixes.summary: contacts bulk-update: a live write needs --yes (no MCP call can set it) or the >100-row digest confirm; batchOutcome counts a row updated only when the batch is COMPLETE and a result names it by the mode's one key (record id for updates, only the --id-property value for upserts, never the JSONL correlation handle); a key empty or shared by two rows of one batch fails those rows; rows rejected while reading count as failures; any unconfirmed row exits 6 unless --allow-partial-failure. handfixes.summary: Every hand-written command orders and compares timestamps chronologically, never as text. One shared rule in novel_helpers.go: cutoffs and bound window edges are rendered by hsTimeString (UTC RFC3339Nano, fractional seconds kept, so a --since/--from with milliseconds is not truncated); every Go sort, latest-pick and cutoff filter goes through hsTimeMillis (hsNewerFirst, hsTimeAfter), which parses RFC3339 with or without a fraction and compares Unix milliseconds rounded like SQLite's julianday(), so a Go compare and a SQL compare of the same values always agree; every SQL compare, MIN, MAX and ORDER BY runs on julianday(), and on the hubspot_property_history column through hsJulianSQL, which also reads the driver's time.Time text (the shape the production writer stores, which bare julianday() reads as NULL). Fail-closed: an empty or unparseable timestamp is unknown, never newer than a cutoff, never the latest, outside every window, and sorts after every real timestamp. Covered: since (cutoff and cross-type sort), engagements of (local ORDER BY, Go sort, live --since filter), notes signals last_note_at, nurture-mine latest_deal_stage (which nurture queue scores on), meetings history order, meetings ever-had and status-report window, first hit and order, deals velocity latest dealstage transition and days_in_stage.
handfixes.why: 2026-10-24 factory Codex review round 2: HubSpot date-times (SimplePublicObject.updatedAt, ValueWithTimestamp.timestamp) arrive as RFC3339 with or without fractional seconds, and '.' sorts before 'Z', so "2026-10-24T14:00:00.500Z" sorts BEFORE "2026-10-24T14:00:00Z" as text. Failing inputs, each a test in hs_review_r2_time_test.go that fails on the pre-fix code: since 2026-10-24T14:00:00.900Z listed a deal updated at 14:00:00.500Z (the cutoff dropped its fraction); since --limit 1 put a 14:00:00Z deal ahead of a 14:00:00.500Z contact; engagements of listed the 14:00:00Z call before the 14:00:00.500Z call; live engagements of --since 2026-10-24T14:00:00Z dropped a call updated at 14:00:00.500Z and kept one with an empty updatedAt; notes signals reported last_note_at 14:00:00Z when a 14:00:00.500Z note existed; nurture-mine reported the stage of the 14:00:00Z deal as latest_deal_stage over the 14:00:00.500Z deal. Property history: the writer binds time.Time, which the driver stores as "2026-10-24 14:00:00.5 +0000 UTC"; that text happens to sort chronologically on its own, but a mirror row in HubSpot's RFC3339 shape sorts after every space-separated row on the same day, so meetings history put a 13:00Z row first, meetings ever-had counted a 08:00Z hit before --from 12:00Z as the first hit, and deals velocity took a 06:00Z transition as the latest over an 08:00 one. A bare julianday() fix would read every writer row as NULL and empty these commands; the history tests also fail under that mutation.

handfixes.summary: Every property HubSpot explicitly returns in an object's top-level properties map (including "" and null) replaces the stored value on every merging write path: generic Upsert, typed Upsert<X>, UpsertBatch (sync pages, the sync --with-history fill, and the live-read and mutation-response write-through), so the resources row and the typed-table data column both carry the clear. A property absent from the response is still kept, and every other key keeps the generated keep-richer policy. The hook is one call in store.go mergeKeepRicherJSON; the rule lives in the hand-authored store/hs_authoritative_properties.go.
handfixes.why: Codex review r2 (P1 with-history snapshot): the generated keep-richer merge keeps the old non-empty value when the incoming value is "" or null, so a HubSpot clear never reached the store. Failing input: deal 1 stored with hubspot_owner_id 7 (an active owner), then `sync --resources hubspot-deals-crm --with-history hubspot_owner_id` returns propertiesWithHistory.hubspot_owner_id newest entry {"value":"","timestamp":"2026-10-24T14:00:00Z","sourceType":"CRM_UI"}; the deal stayed owned by 7 and `deals unowned --json` omitted it. The same loss hit a regular sync returning "hubspot_owner_id":"" or null in properties, and the write-through of a PATCH response after `patch ... --properties '{"hubspot_owner_id":""}'` (HubSpot documents clearing a property by passing ""). Tests: TestR2HistoryClearSurvivesTheStoreMerge, TestR2HistoryClearShowsInDealsUnowned, TestR2ReturnedPropertyClearSurvivesTheStoreMerge, TestR2PatchClearReachesTheLocalMirror (internal/cli), TestAuthoritativePropertiesSurviveEveryUpsertPath, TestMergeKeepRicherJSONHubSpotPropertiesScope (internal/store).

The only exemption is an exact pp:path allowlist of POSTs that read (object search and batch read, property and association batch read, list search, list membership batch read). A --yes saved in a run profile does not count. Gated commands' help examples are rewritten to carry --dry-run / --yes. contacts bulk-update keeps its own --yes and digest gate.

handfixes.summary: A run profile saves and applies only the flags on an explicit allowlist (runProfileAllowedFlags: output and format flags, read source and freshness, and filters that appear only on read commands). Every other flag, every approval flag (--yes, --confirm, --digest, any future one) included, is never saved (profile save names what it left out) and never applied (a profile file that carries one gets a stderr warning and the value is ignored), so no saved profile can approve, shape or redirect a write.
handfixes.why: Codex round 1 (publish lane, 2026-10-24): after `profile save always-yes --yes`, `contacts bulk-update --jsonl --profile always-yes` sent a live update without confirmation; the bulk-update gate read the profile-applied flags.yes. Codex round 2 (2026-10-26) repeated the class: reserving only yes still let a profile file's --confirm/--digest approve a 101-row bulk update. The denylist became an allowlist.

The fleet tool for this class will not merge (owner decision 2026-10-28), so the connector closes it by hand. Known limits: a guessable override can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; text that carries no held value (a recall query) is kept as the press designs it.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal (SecretEnv HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN and HUBSPOT_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN; Files = the one file the program discovers its base URL in (config.BaseURLFile, with --home read by the CLI's own command tree; the kit takes the base URL from an explicit --config over it), every other file a run may read held directly through config.HoldFile so its base_url cannot become the allowed origin; ConfigFields auth_header, access_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret; BaseURL base_url / HUBSPOT_BASE_URL / https://api.hubapi.com; every credential bound to the base_url origin, the MCP bearer and the TLS key to none). The MCP server holds every value --tls-key could have before it parses flags. internal/cli/hs_profile_hold.go holds what a run profile store carries as a credential at startup: a value under a credential's name or under base-url, every duplicate included (free text is not a source). internal/credsql registers the one credkit-sqlite driver, with the MCP sql tool's value cap set as each connection opens. credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit ends them. Every sink is routed: stdout and stderr at the descriptor, the API client's cliutil.OutboundGuard, deliver, feedback and the auth probe through credkit.Transport, cache, journal, teach log, profile and export files through credkit.WriteFile, AppendFile, OpenFile and NewWriter, the MCP server through MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP, child processes through RunCommand and StartCommand. The connector's own 0600 credential store and config file are credential sources: their writes stay outside the kit in cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile.
handfixes.why: Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, secret-echo-success-bodies and secret-echo-held-chokepoint, replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements fleet_handfixes.json backs). That filter kept growing per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time. The kit is one shared implementation of the leak contract, checked byte for byte against tools/maintainer/credkit (vendor_credkit.py --check). A match withholds the whole unit, and a credentialed request over plain http or to another origin is refused. Local files the connector writes that carry no credential by construction (lock files, the fingerprint key, the SQLite journal stub) are not routed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the press should vendor the kit and generate the Start and Exit lines and the sink routing, so a reprint keeps them.
